name: Hirschsprung Disease-Deafness-Polydactyly Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Hirschsprung Disease-Deafness-Polydactyly Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital aganglionic megacolon (Hirschsprung disease) confirmed by rectal biopsy
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss documented by audiometry
Presence of postaxial polydactyly of hands and/or feet
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes (e.g., RET or other candidate genes)
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: congenital Hirschsprung disease, bilateral sensorineural deafness, and postaxial polydactyly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical triad is essential.

laboratory: Rectal suction biopsy showing absence of ganglion cells
Audiometric testing confirming bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
imaging: Contrast enema demonstrating transition zone in colon
Ultrasound or MRI for polydactyly and associated musculoskeletal anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in RET gene or other candidate genes associated with Hirschsprung disease
Genetic testing for syndromic polydactyly and deafness genes
other: Family history assessment for inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of sensorineural deafness and polydactyly
Presence of retinal dystrophy and obesity
Polydactyly with renal anomalies but typically no Hirschsprung disease
Craniofacial microsomia and ear anomalies without Hirschsprung disease

redFlags: Neonatal intestinal obstruction with delayed meconium passage
Presence of extra digits (postaxial polydactyly) at birth
references: Am J Med Genet. 1995;57(3):298-302. Clinical and genetic aspects of Hirschsprung disease-deafness-polydactyly syndrome
